notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 80-year-old female admitted for upper GI bleed. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.45, creatinine 0.99-1.01, hemoglobin 12.1-13.6, platelets 263-266, sodium 140, wbc 6.6-7.2; vitals dbp 74-79, heart_rate 68-73, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 14-16, sbp 125-133, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: EGD: bleeding duodenal ulcer, treated with endoscopic clips; Pantoprazole 80 mg IV
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Anemia.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.99-1.05, hemoglobin 11-12, platelets 258-267, sodium 140, wbc 6.9-7.2; vitals dbp 74-79, heart_rate 68-72, map 91-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 125-132, spo2 96-97, temp 36.9-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Transfuse 1 unit packed red blood cells
Assessment and plan: Upper GI bleed. Anemia. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 80-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Upper GI bleed. Anemia. Follow up with primary care in one week. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed.
